 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Taylor Fritz is putting his Miami real estate on the market, listing his condominium at Hyde Midtown for $860,000. The American tennis star purchased the property for $845,000 in March 2023, meaning his asking price is $15,000 higher after more than three years of ownership.
 According to the Realtor.com report on Fritz's Miami condo listing , the residence covers 1,096 square feet and features two bedrooms and two bathrooms. Located in the Hyde Midtown complex, the corner unit offers eastern and southern exposures, with floor-to-ceiling impact-resistant glass providing views of the Miami skyline and Biscayne Bay.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The property also features an open-plan living and dining area, a modern kitchen with integrated appliances and a wraparound balcony. The primary bedroom has direct access to the terrace and a custom walk-in closet.
 The building offers several amenities, including a heated swimming pool, spa, fitness center, media rooms and a private tennis court. Residents also have access to valet parking, 24-hour security and communal recreational spaces.
 Fritz's asking price represents an approximately 1.8% increase over his original purchase price. However, the property's $1,820 monthly homeowners association fee adds a considerable recurring expense. That amounts to $21,840 annually, before property taxes, maintenance and other ownership costs.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Christopher O'Connell (AUS) Aaron Doster-Imagn Images
 The listing is being handled by Elaine Atkins of Coldwell Banker Realty. Buyers can also use the property as a rental investment, with listing materials permitting leases of at least 30 days up to 12 times annually.
 Fritz purchased the condominium before reaching a major milestone in his tennis career. In September 2024, he advanced to his first Grand Slam singles final at the U.S. Open after defeating fellow American Frances Tiafoe in the semifinals. He eventually finished runner-up to Jannik Sinner.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Miami listing has also attracted attention from other outlets, including MarketWatch's coverage of the $860,000 property and SSBCrack's report on the tennis star's real estate move .
 For Fritz, the sale would mark a change in his Miami property holdings, with the condominium now being offered above its original purchase price.
